PakWheels is back with another owner's review. This time, we bring a farewell video in honour of the Suzuki Mehran VXR along with its specs, features and price in Pakistan.

Suzuki Mehran Car belongs to the 2nd generation which was introduced in 2012. The 2nd generation of Suzuki Mehran Car featured a series of minor cosmetic upgrades and an engine upgrade that made it Euro II compliant. The remaining aspects of the Mehran Car are identical to the 1st generation. However, all the variants will now come with an Immobilizer. The Suzuki Mehran Car comes in 4 variants Mehran VX, VX CNG, VXR and VXR CNG.
________________________________________________
Exterior
The Suzuki Mehran exterior features a fairly box like design. Mehran Car front end features the use of trapezium shaped headlights with a grille that features multiple rectangular shaped openings on one side and a sealed end on the other along with standard black bumpers. The rear end of car houses slightly angular squared shaped taillights, a standard hatchback along with a standard black bumper. On the higher end Mehran VXR variants, the Mehran Car comes equipped with color matched bumpers and full wheel covers. The overall exterior of the Suzuki Mehran features a restrained and minimalistic design language that is typical for a car designed in the eighties.

0.8 Liter OHC 6 Valve Inline-3

4 Speed Manual Transmission

Mileage
The Suzuki Mehran 2019 gives an average mileage of 10 KM/L in city making for an estimated range of 300 KM from its 30-litre fuel tank and 13KM/L on the highway making for an estimated range of 390 KM on a highway.

He also shares his experience of taking the Wagon R on a northern trip, where the car performed well without feeling underpowered. He appreciates the generous headroom, decent legroom, powerful air conditioning, and rates the infotainment system highly.

Muaz also discusses the car's fuel average before highlighting a few drawbacks. He experienced noise from the front suspension, although the issue resolved itself over time. He also mentions the absence of rear power windows and auto-folding side mirrors as missing features.

Towards the end of the review, Muaz says spare parts are readily available in the market, although maintenance costs have increased over time. He also shares that PakWheels has been very helpful in comparing cars and making informed ownership decisions.
